thesis: The business is doing well - AWS grew 37% in Q2 2026, its fastest in 18 quarters - but the stock has done nothing for five weeks since the +15% earnings pop and the packet shows it as the weakest of our US holdings: RSI 47, 3m momentum +5.1%, no breakout. A good company at a price that is not moving, with no catalyst until late October, is a hold, not a buy. No edge here today.
bull_case: Q2 2026 (30 Jul 2026): net sales $200.6B, +20% y/y, ahead of $197.01B consensus; operating income $27.5B, +43% y/y, margin 13.7%; AWS $42.2B, +37% y/y - the fastest in 18 quarters - with AWS operating income $16.6B at a 39.4% margin, up from $10.2B a year earlier. AWS AI and its in-house chips each passed $25B annualised, more than doubling. Advertising $19.8B, +26%. Shares rose ~15% on 31 Jul and the market cap passed $3T. Packet has close above SMA50 above SMA200, so the long-term trend is intact.
bear_case: Trailing-twelve-month property and equipment purchases hit $169B, up 64% y/y. That is the entire bear case in one number: AWS growth is being bought, and free cash flow is the bill. Price behaviour agrees that the market has stopped paying up - RSI 47, 3m momentum +5.1% versus NVDA at +12.3% and MSFT at +20.2%, no 55-day breakout, score only +0.40. The next company catalyst is late-Oct results. Meanwhile a 16 Sep Fed hike and a 10-year near 4.8% are a direct headwind to a capex-heavy compounder. I found no manipulation, delisting or accounting red flags.
catalysts: Q3 2026 results late Oct 2026: AWS growth rate and capex guidance
16 Sep 2026 FOMC and the direction of long yields
risks: Capex up 64% y/y compressing free cash flow
AWS growth decelerating from the 37% peak
Consumer weakness if the energy-driven inflation impulse persists
Rate sensitivity of a long-duration compounder
invalidation: Flips to long on a daily close above 272 (a new 55-day high) with AWS growth confirmed above 35% at the October print; flips to negative on a close below 240, which breaks the SMA50 structure.
